research_question: In women undergoing hysterectomy for benign gynaecological disease, does a laparoscopic approach (laparoscopically assisted vaginal hysterectomy, total laparoscopic hysterectomy, or laparoscopic hysterectomy of unspecified type), compared with vaginal hysterectomy, change the odds of requiring a blood transfusion during the operation and hospital stay or up to the end of follow-up?
treatment_label: Laparoscopic hysterectomy (LAVH, TLH, or laparoscopic hysterectomy of unspecified type)
outcome_description: Number of women who received a blood transfusion (any transfusion, intra-operative or post-operative) out of the number randomised to each arm, recorded during the operation and the hospital stay or up to the end of follow-up. Events and arm totals are extracted as counts; the number randomised is the denominator (intention-to-treat). Blood loss volume, haemoglobin drop, and haematoma are not used. Trials with zero transfusions in both arms are recorded as zero-event rows with their arm sizes. In multi-arm trials comparing more than one laparoscopic approach with a single vaginal hysterectomy group, each laparoscopic approach forms its own comparison and the vaginal group's size and events are split equally between them. Abdominal and robotic hysterectomy arms are ignored.
positive_direction: An odds ratio greater than 1 means MORE women required a blood transfusion in the laparoscopic hysterectomy group than in the vaginal hysterectomy group (i.e. a result unfavourable to laparoscopic hysterectomy); an OR below 1 means fewer transfusions with laparoscopic hysterectomy.
search_queries: laparoscopic hysterectomy versus vaginal hysterectomy randomised controlled trial benign disease
laparoscopically assisted vaginal hysterectomy trial blood transfusion complications
total laparoscopic hysterectomy vaginal hysterectomy comparison surgical outcomes trial
inclusion_criteria: Randomised controlled trial in women undergoing hysterectomy for benign gynaecological disease
Compares a laparoscopic approach to hysterectomy (LAVH, TLH, or unspecified laparoscopic) with vaginal hysterectomy
Reports some quantitative peri-operative outcome data, including blood transfusion counts (or zero events) per arm
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, editorial, opinion piece, narrative review, or purely theoretical/protocol paper)
No comparison between a laparoscopic hysterectomy arm and a vaginal hysterectomy control arm (e.g. only abdominal or robotic hysterectomy comparators), or non-randomised design
No quantitative outcome data from which an effect size can be computed (no event counts/proportions, means+SDs, t/F values, or odds ratios)
Completely unrelated to the research topic (e.g. hysterectomy for malignancy, non-hysterectomy gynaecological surgery)
moderators_to_extract: Type of laparoscopic approach (LAVH vs TLH vs unspecified)
Primary indication (fibroids, prolapse, abnormal bleeding, mixed)
Risk of bias / allocation concealment adequacy
effect_size_note: Pool as an odds ratio using a fixed-effect Mantel-Haenszel model where available, otherwise random effects. Compute the OR directly from event counts with laparoscopic hysterectomy as the treatment group and vaginal hysterectomy as the control group; assign arms by procedure description, not column position. Double-zero trials are retained as visible rows but contribute no weight. Do not pool operating time, hospital stay, other complications, return to normal activities, conversion to laparotomy, pain, or cost.
